title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: detect sensitivity labels on files inside archives
summary: The briefing accurately separates Microsoft's planned archive-label detection change from documented Endpoint DLP capabilities. The roadmap dates, existing controls and licensing are supported, and searches did not find published defaults or a dedicated switch for this change.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; controls[0].scope; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Centrally configured Endpoint DLP settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.
claims.quote: Centrally configured settings control many aspects of endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) behavior. These settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.

claims.claim: Endpoint settings include Disable classification for specific file extensions.
claims.quote:
## Disable classification
Use this setting to exclude specific file extensions from Endpoint DLP classification.

claims.claim: Disable classification excludes extensions on the Monitored files list from content scanning.
claims.quote: For files that are on the [Monitored files](/en-us/purview/endpoint-dlp-learn-about) list, you can disable classification through this setting. When you add a file extension to this setting, Endpoint DLP doesn't scan content in files with this extension.

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

You can use [sensitivity labels](sensitivity-labels) as a condition in DLP policies for these locations:

- OneDrive
- Devices
